listenings.text: Leonardo, it is Claire Whitmore. I got your two pages and I read them on the train, which is the best review I can give you. Two things before Thursday. First, the answer is clear and I could follow it from the first line to the last, so whatever you changed since January, keep doing that. Second, and I want to be direct about it. The third paragraph does not address the question I asked. It is accurate. It is also about the two thousand and twenty-one file, and I did not ask about the two thousand and twenty-one file. If the board reads that paragraph, they will think we are defending something. Cut it, or move it to an annex. One more thing, and this is not a criticism. You use the word significant four times on page one. Pick a different word three times, or pick a number. A number is never vague. I will be on the call at nine, and I will have the chairman with me, which I know you enjoy.

I have marked this examination for eleven years, and I want to tell you the one thing that separates the candidates who pass comfortably from the ones who fail by two marks. It is not vocabulary. The ones who fail by two marks read the question last. They read the passage carefully, from the first word, the way you would read a contract, and then they meet the question and they have to go back. That is four minutes gone, on a paper where you have seventy-five. So read the question first. Then skim the passage for the shape of it, thirty seconds, no more, and only then go looking for the answer. And when you go looking, remember what the paper is doing to you. The correct option almost never uses the words of the passage. It paraphrases them. So a candidate who is hunting for matching words is being led, on purpose, to the wrong answer. Two more things. If a question asks what the writer implies, the answer is not written down anywhere, and reading harder will not find it. And in the written part, nobody is counting your ideas. The examiner is asking whether your second sentence follows your first. One clear idea, defended, beats three ideas mentioned.

extra_audio.text: In my view, the rules are too complex for a foreign investor to navigate alone. This is supported by the fact that three separate authorities can review the same payment. One could argue that professional advice already solves the problem. However, it should be noted that the cost of that advice falls on the smallest investors. In conclusion, the evidence suggests that simplification would open the market rather than close it.

reading.rtitle: Reading Set · Passage A: industry note · Passage B: reply from the compliance director
paras: Passage A, industry note, fourteenth of March. Foreign fintechs entering Brazil have been told for years that the main obstacle is the rate. The rate is not the obstacle. What stops most of them is that a single intercompany payment can be looked at by three different authorities, each with its own guidance, and none of them obliged to agree with the others. A company that has been advised well will price the transaction once and document it three times. A company that has not will find out about the difference eighteen months later, when the assessment arrives and the file has to be rebuilt from memory.

The note closes with a recommendation that surprised nobody in the market: firms should narrow down their structures before the reform is implemented, not after. What surprised the market was the second half of that sentence. The author, a former tax authority official, wrote that the groups most exposed today are not the newcomers. They are the groups that restructured early, in 2021, and have not opened the file since.

Passage B, from Claire Whitmore, compliance director. Thank you for the note. I agree with most of it, and I want to be careful about one line. You write that early restructuring is now the bigger exposure. That is true for groups that never revisited the file, and it is the opposite of true for us: the pricing has been reviewed every year since 2021 and the documentation was rebuilt in January. What I would like from your team is not another note. It is a two-page answer to one question: if the reform is implemented in the form published last month, does our current structure still hold? Please cut to the chase. I have to present this to a board that reads the first paragraph and stops.
reading.source: Exam-format reading set built from an industry note and a client reply (adapted for class)

gist.prompt: Skim once, thirty seconds. What is the best title for this reading set?
choices: A history of fintech regulation in Brazil since 2021
Why the rate is not the obstacle, and which groups are most exposed
Instructions for filing an intercompany payment return

items: The industry note argues that the tax rate is the main obstacle for foreign fintechs.
The note says the opposite: what stops them is that one payment can be reviewed by three authorities that are not obliged to agree.
According to the note, the groups most exposed are the ones that restructured in 2021 and never opened the file again.
That is the second half of the sentence, and it is the part that surprised the market.
Claire Whitmore rejects the industry note.
She agrees with most of it and objects to one line only, because her own pricing has been reviewed every year since 2021.
Claire Whitmore asks the team for a longer, more detailed note.
She asks for a two-page answer to one question and tells the team to cut to the chase.
